application.cover_letter_markdown:
For the past seven years at Tuulikallio Embedded Systems I have been designing and delivering digital signal-processing products for industrial and scientific instrumentation. The central project was the TWDR-4 wideband digital receiver: a 16-channel beamforming system that I took from algorithm design through to a shipping embedded implementation on Xilinx Zynq hardware. Two units are in the field with paying customers. Your posting for a Senior Signal Processing Engineer at Kaikuvaara describes essentially the same kind of work, and that is why I am writing.

The TWDR-4 was a full-chain effort. The processing pipeline handles per-channel digital down-conversion, time-delay beamforming with adaptive weight computation, and real-time output under a hard 2 ms latency ceiling. I wrote the firmware in C under bare-metal scheduling on the Zynq's ARM core, and I also handled the acceptance-test measurements on each unit before delivery. The RF measurement skills behind that testing trace back to my MSc at Tampere, where I ran antenna pattern measurements, network-analyser calibration, and LNA noise-figure characterisation for a university ground-station project -- practical bench work that I have used continuously since.

One thing the CV does not fully convey is the Python infrastructure work I have done. At Tuulikallio I wrote and now maintain the automated calibration-verification and regression-test framework that the integration team runs against every product build. It is about 8,000 lines of Python, tested with pytest, version-controlled, CI-gated, and used daily by five engineers besides myself. The system handles instrument control, data acquisition, comparison against golden datasets, and report generation. It began as a quick script and I turned it into something the team cannot ship without. That is production software in every practical sense.

I have been in Oulu since 2019, having relocated specifically for the position at Tuulikallio. The city's RF and signal-processing ecosystem is what brought me here, and I have no intention of leaving. Kaikuvaara's work on remote-sensing instruments is a natural extension of what I have been building at Tuulikallio, and I would appreciate the chance to discuss it.

Erik Berg

application.cover_letter_markdown:
Twenty-one years at one company, and I am applying to leave. Let me explain why.

I joined Hallaharju Space Systems straight out of KUT in 2005. Over the years I have worked on every part of the signal-processing chain: embedded firmware on SHARC DSPs, RF front-end measurement and calibration, the Python test and data-management platform, beamformer algorithm design, and for the last eight years leading the signal-processing group through three product generations. That is honest work, but after this long I am not willing to spend the next decade doing it. I need problems that are still open.

Kaikuvaara caught my eye because your core business -- remote-sensing instrumentation -- puts signal processing at the heart of the product rather than behind it. The skills your posting asks for are an unusually close match to what I have been building: wideband digital receiver design, beamforming, embedded DSP on production hardware, RF bench measurement, and the engineering-quality tooling that ties it all together. I have not often seen a posting that maps this directly onto my actual work history.

On the practical side, I live in Oulu and intend to stay. I am not interested in remote work and I do not need to relocate. That Kaikuvaara is local is a genuine draw rather than a coincidence -- the instrumentation cluster in this city is part of why I have stayed here for fourteen years.

I am available for a conversation whenever works for you.

Pekka Nieminen

As a highly motivated and results-oriented signal processing professional, I believe my unique combination of technical depth and strategic thinking would make me an outstanding addition to your world-class team developing mission-critical remote-sensing instrumentation.

The work that Kaikuvaara does in spaceborne and airborne radar and optical payload signal processing is exactly the kind of high-impact, technically demanding engineering that defines where I want to be. I am also a proven leader. I thrive when leading cross-functional engineering teams in collaborative, high-stakes environments, and I have consistently demonstrated my ability to drive projects forward while maintaining rigorous standards of technical quality. I believe in knowledge sharing, mentorship, and creating a team culture where every member delivers their best work.

At Tuulenkaari I have been immersed in signal processing work that has sharpened my capabilities across multiple domains. My core competencies include phased-array and beamforming techniques, hands-on RF measurement, and production-quality Python development, all of which I apply regularly. I have also made meaningful contributions to open-source projects, reflecting my commitment to the broader engineering community.

What sets me apart is the combination of deep technical competence with genuine strategic vision and leadership ability. I do not simply solve signal processing problems -- I anticipate them, architect solutions proactively, and build systems that are robust, scalable, and production-ready from day one.

I am based in Oulu and ready to hit the ground running at Kaikuvaara. I would welcome the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your team.

Best regards,
Kari Heinonen

application.cover_letter_markdown:
There are things in my background that match what you are looking for, and things that do not, and I would rather be upfront about both than leave you to work it out from the CV.

For the past ten years at Hallaharju Space Systems I have worked on the simulation and verification side of signal processing -- building MATLAB-based signal chain models, designing simulation test cases against system requirements, writing verification reports, and maintaining the test infrastructure that catches problems before they ship. It is not the most visible engineering work, but it is work I do well and take seriously.

The area where my experience connects most directly to your posting is beamforming, and I should be specific about that because the evidence comes from a personal project rather than my day job. Last year I built a four-microphone array beamforming demonstrator: a delay-and-sum beamsteering setup using MEMS microphone breakout boards connected through a USB audio interface, with the beamforming computation running in MATLAB on a laptop. I characterised the array's directivity pattern by placing a calibration source on a rotating platform at one-metre distance and sweeping the delay weights across a 180-degree arc. I measured the beam patterns, computed the sidelobe levels, and got the setup tracking a moving source in real time using a streaming audio input. This was not paid work and it was not peer-reviewed, but it was genuine engineering: delay-line computation, spatial weight optimisation, array calibration, and pattern measurement. The principles are the same ones your phased-array instrument work rests on, just at a different scale and a lower frequency.

I want to be honest about the gaps as well. My professional experience has been simulation-oriented and heavily MATLAB-based. My formal degree is in industrial engineering, not in electrical engineering or physics, and there are areas in your posting where I simply do not have the track record you are most likely looking for. I am not trying to paper over that.

What I am hoping is that a decade of disciplined signal-processing verification work, a solid quantitative foundation, and a genuine personal investment in beamforming engineering is enough to warrant a conversation. I am currently working from Hallaharju Space Systems' Oulu office on a project assignment and would be happy to take a permanent position in the city. The kind of hands-on remote-sensing instrument work that Kaikuvaara does is where I want to take my career, and I would rather make that argument in person than try to fit it into a letter. I recognise the gaps are real, but I think the conversation would be worthwhile.

Thank you for considering my application.

Nadia Nowak

Klara Petrov

application.cover_letter_markdown:
What drew me to this posting, honestly, is the company's place in the Oulu RF and photonics engineering cluster. I have been watching the signal processing and instrument ecosystem there from a professional standpoint for several years now -- the university's wireless research groups, Suvanto's antenna and photonics work, the cluster of sensor and instrument companies that draw from the same talent pool. It is one of the strongest concentrations of RF engineering expertise in Northern Europe, and Kaikuvaara is at the heart of it. For an engineer whose daily work is RF characterisation and measurement, that is a compelling environment to think about.

I have been at Hallaharju Space Systems since completing my MSc in Electrical Engineering at Kallavesi in 2019. My role is in the RF test and characterisation group, where I spend most of my time on component-level RF measurements: S-parameter sweeps across frequency and temperature, noise-figure verification, gain-flatness characterisation, and linearity testing, all using Rohde & Schwarz vector network analysers and signal analysers. It is methodical, detail-oriented bench work that requires patience and precision, and it is where my strengths lie.

The connection between my education and my current work is direct. My MSc thesis was on wideband impedance matching for multi-stage RF amplifier chains -- the kind of front-end design problem that comes up constantly in receiver characterisation for instrument companies. That theoretical foundation underpins the measurement judgments I make every day about what is and is not within specification.

I also have a working familiarity with Kalman filtering and estimation theory, which I understand has relevance to the tracking and state-estimation aspects of remote-sensing signal processing.

I want to be straightforward about the scope of my experience. My work has been focused on RF component characterisation and test-bench measurement for the past six years. I have not done phased-array algorithm design, and my strength is squarely on the measurement and characterisation side. I am applying because I believe instrument companies need that expertise, but I do not want to create an impression of breadth that I do not have.

The Oulu RF community is something I have followed with genuine interest for some time. The depth of antenna, radar, and millimetre-wave work happening there is difficult to match elsewhere in Finland, and Kaikuvaara's position in that ecosystem is what makes this role particularly interesting to me.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my RF measurement background might contribute to your team.

Stefan Horvath
